text: I saw a tick tock a long time ago that just absolutely amazed me but I just want to share it here and this is what
the tick tock said all right let's see it there was a moment in time when Moses had the courage to ask God what his name is
God answered in the name he gave is recorded in the original Hebrew as yhwh over time humans have added a and an e
in his name to get Yahweh presumably because we have a preference for vowels so humans did not simply add vowels to a
name that did not originally contain vowels Scholars have worked for many centuries to try to reconstruct how the
Divine name the tetragrammaton was originally pronounced and the challenge is that ancient Hebrew and even modern Hebrew is not written with vowels that
does not mean that the language doesn't use vowels there has never been a single moment in the history of the Hebrew
language during which vowels were not pronounced that is true of the Divine name that is true of every other syllable of the entire Hebrew Bible
which was originally written without vowels the notion that the Divine name was ever pronounced without vowels is
pure and utter nonsense but Scholars and rabbis have noted that the letters y-h-wh represent breathing sounds so
these claims are entirely false this is not something that was produced by Scholars this is something that was produced by people who do not have a
firm grasp of the biology or the Linguistics involved and these are consonants and they are made by moving
your tongue and your throat and your lips in very specific very precise ways to produce these sounds that are
entirely unrelated to the physiology and the phonology of normal human breathing
when said without intervening vowels it sounds like this consonants are not pronounced without
vowels in Hebrew and that's absolutely not the sound that these consonants make perhaps this is why yhwh was considered
an unspeakable name because quite literally it is not supposed to be spoken but breathed the notion that
tetragrammaton was intended to be breathed and not pronounced is an entirely modern and profoundly naive misunderstanding of the Hebrew language
that has absolutely no relationship with the development of a taboo regarding the pronunciation of the Divine name in
second temple Judaism
